newsitem.title: FRANCE: Details of Air France alliance plans.
newsitem.headline: Details of Air France alliance plans.

text.p: Air France, confirming alliances with Delta Air Lines Inc and Continental Airlines, said the link-ups would widen each partner's market access and improve services for both passengers and freight.
France's state airline said the two letters of intent signed with the U.S. carriers included plans for "code-sharing," or through-ticketing, subject to government approval.
More than three million passengers fly between France and the United States each year, making it the third biggest transatlantic market, Air France said.
No financial information was available but Air France gave the following details.

-- Delta and Air France are to study the possibility for cooperation in the following areas: improved passenger and freight connections, computer reservations, cooperation and assistance at airports and coordinated sales and marketing.
-- The airlines plan closer coordination of flight schedules and code-sharing between the United States and France, but this is subject to government approval.
-- Air France said the terms of this deal were similar. It covered both passenger and freight connections, reservation systems, airport assistance and sales and marketing.
-- It also included code-sharing between France and the United States as well as "points beyond the hubs of each partner". As with the Delta agreement, this idea is subject to official approval.
Air France said both agreements would grant the partners access to markets which they by themselves currently serve more seldom than once a day or not at all.
Delta operates from its hub at Atlanta, Georgia, while Continental works from Houston, Texas, and Air France uses Paris Roissy-Charles De Gaulle airport.
